note: Steps that must run in the ordered build job rather than in a shard, because they are sensitive to WHERE in the profile they run - not merely to having a built tree. This file is the LAST of three layers, and normally stays empty. Layer one: a step that writes a snapshot is a producer whatever its command is called, so it runs in the ordered build job. Layer two: steps whose ids differ only by a role suffix (-snapshot/-check/-verify/-apply/-self-test) form a family, and a family containing a producer is moved into the ordered build job whole, while a wholly shardable family is packed as one indivisible unit - both derived from the matrix at run time, so a new pair is handled with no edit here. Layer three is this file, for a step that is order-sensitive for a reason no naming convention reveals. A pin only MOVES a step; `verify` reconciles the build job's receipt together with the shard receipts against all the steps the profile declares, so nothing here can remove a step from the run, a pin naming a step the profile no longer declares is refused, and a pin without a reason is refused.

ordered_steps.reason: Kept as belt-and-braces over the derived rules, because this pair has already failed once in this repo in a way that reported green. The snapshot once ran at profile step 44 and the check that read it at step 58, so the guard compared against a baseline written after the steps it was meant to police - it graded its own answer sheet and could not fail. That was fixed by moving the pair ahead of build:all, to indices 5 and 6. Sharding is a second chance to reintroduce it in a new form: each shard unpacks its own copy of the tree, so a check on a different runner than its snapshot would again compare against a baseline that runner had just written. Run 33393681323 showed the milder version of the same mistake - the check alone was hoisted past build:all and reported 168 changed surfaces, failing for a reason that was not real - and run 33394734639 showed the inverse, the snapshot alone landing in a shard. Both members belong in the ordered build job, adjacent, in matrix order.
